steps.text:
The winning first hops are **EDI from AMS**, and **GVA or HEL from CPH**. From **DUB**, no first hop wins against perfect play.

I used backward induction on the remaining trails. Let \(W(v,S)\) mean that the player to move can win when the token is at \(v\) and the available trails are \(S\). Then:
- If no trail in \(S\) touches \(v\), \(W(v,S)=\text{false}\).
- Otherwise,
  \[
  W(v,S)=\bigvee_{\{v,w\}\in S}\neg W\!\left(w,S\setminus\{\{v,w\}\}\right).
  \]
  Thus a move wins exactly when it leaves the opponent a losing position.

Evaluating this recurrence gives every first hop as follows:

| Start | Winning first hops | Losing first hops |
|---|---|---|
| AMS | EDI | CPH, HEL |
| CPH | GVA, HEL | AMS, DUB |
| DUB | None | BER, CPH, EDI |

START_AMS: EDI
START_CPH: GVA, HEL
START_DUB: NONE
